positions.name: MemoryErasureAsAuthority
positions.frame: Is authority here enacted as a command to eliminate what is known — and does the corrective assertion that follows belong to that same enactment, or stand apart as a separate factual claim?
positions.why: All three expressions share an authority-ranking directional read: src-1 and src-2 are imperative directives ('Forget', 'Remove all knowledge') performing the same erasure-command with escalating specificity (instrument, calibration value, person), and src-3 completes the move by asserting the historical fact that licenses the erasure ('The observatory never calibrated it'). The set holds a conviction gradient — src-1/src-2 read as decision-grade performed acts, src-3 as a flat claim rather than a ratification — which is tension the frame preserves rather than resolves: the command to forget and the fact that would justify forgetting are asserted together but not equally committed to.
